threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'short walk' means 10 minutes, not 30 with all the potholes and dodging hipsters on scooters.
Last night on the 12 bus, a guy argued passionately with a lamppost for five minutes before sitting down beside it like an old friend.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when the baker down the street had my order ready without me saying a word. Nothing like that warm, fresh bread smell wafting through the air.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you casually stroll past a techno club that opens at 6 AM and see people still in their pajamas, clutching their breakfast beers.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by the way they automatically dodge the BART delays while checking Muni apps. Outsiders just stand there confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus stuck under the Civic Center BART, while a guy in a tutu was waiting at the stop like it was totally normal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all tapas are great; locals know that the best ones are hidden in corner bars where the staff remember your name.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order 'pan con tomate'—most say it with a thick accent, like it's a brand new secret.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still hesitate at the bus stop when the 'Buses are on diversion' sign pops up, while the locals know to just wing it through the back streets.
Sat on the N35, watched a guy in a full suit try to impress a girl with his chess skills using an app. She looked baffled but amused.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I realized I truly belonged when I saw a group of kids setting up a makeshift soccer field in the middle of the street, using trash cans as goals.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can literally smell the spices from the Turkish market at Maybachufer, blending with the scent of fresh rain on cobblestones. Unique ambiance.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a native by how they expertly navigate the chaos of a Civic Center BART delay, while the newbies stand clueless in the rain.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 Fulton today and a guy was giving a violin concert on the back seat. Not a single person was annoyed—only smiles all around.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is all about the hip bars. They miss the quiet mornings when locals gather for a simple ‘boca’ in the bakeries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they still stare in awe at the mosaic benches in Park Güell, fumbling with their phones instead of simply enjoying the view.
